title_prefix: Script ASM renders small pushes as hex a
mechanism: DISASSEMBLE-SCRIPT (src/validation/script.lisp:573-650) renders every data push through bl.crypto:bytes-to-hex regardless of length and every non-push opcode through the *OPCODE-NAMES* table, which spells OP_0, OP_1NEGATE and OP_1..OP_16. Core's ScriptToAsmStr (refs/bitcoin/src/core_io.cpp:357-401) renders a push of four bytes or fewer as the DECIMAL CScriptNum value and only longer pushes as hex, and GetOpName (script/script.cpp:23-44) returns '0' for OP_0, '-1' for OP_1NEGATE and '1'..'16' for OP_1..OP_16. Core also has the fAttemptSighashDecode branch, which TxToUniv passes for every scriptSig: a push passing CheckSignatureEncoding has its trailing sighash byte removed and replaced by a '[ALL]'-style suffix. We have no sighash decoding at all, and the same function serves scriptPubKey and scriptSig, so there is no place to pass the flag.
consequence: Every asm field the node emits differs from Core for any script containing a small push or a small-number opcode, which is very nearly all of them - decodescript, decoderawtransaction, getrawtransaction verbose, getblock verbosity 2 and 3, gettxout, scantxoutset, the PSBT decoders, the REST surfaces and the web UI all render through this one function. A CLTV height reads as raw little-endian hex instead of a block number, tooling that matches '0 <20-byte hash>' to recognise a v0 witness program sees 'OP_0 ...', and every scriptSig signature keeps its sighash byte where Core shows the type. It is nevertheless a field-content divergence and nothing else: the hex fields, the addresses, the types and the txids are all correct, and no caller is handed a wrong fee, transaction or address to act on. Confirmed as a mechanism and downgraded to S3 on the consequence; its breadth, not its severity, is the argument for fixing it early.
evidence: Probe ga11v-rpcutil-p2 (scratch, not committed) *GA11-P2-ASM*: fourteen vectors taken from Core's own rpc_decodescript.py assertions, run through bl.val:disassemble-script. 13 of 14 differ. '5100' -> ours 'OP_1 OP_0', Core '1 0' (rpc_decodescript.py:53). The CLTV redeem script -> ours '... OP_ELSE 20a107 OP_CHECKLOCKTIMEVERIFY ...', Core '... OP_ELSE 500000 OP_CHECKLOCKTIMEVERIFY ...' (:136). P2WPKH '0014<20>' -> ours 'OP_0 a1b2...', Core '0 a1b2...' (:166). P2TR '5120<32>' -> ours 'OP_1 1111...', Core '1 1111...' (:187). The anchor '51024e73' -> ours 'OP_1 4e73', Core '1 29518' (:197, and the test spells out that the witness program is shown as a single decimal). Bare pushes: '0164' -> '64' vs '100'; '026400' -> '6400' vs '100'; '0320a107' -> '20a107' vs '500000'; '0401020304' -> '01020304' vs '67305985'. OP_1NEGATE -> 'OP_1NEGATE' vs '-1'. The 2-of-3 multisig -> 'OP_2 ... OP_3 OP_CHECKMULTISIG' vs '2 ... 3 OP_CHECKMULTISIG' (:93). A pushed signature -> the bare 71-byte hex where Core appends '[ALL]' after stripping the sighash byte (:210). The one match is the >4-byte OP_RETURN push (:117), which both render as hex - the positive control that the probe is comparing real output and not failing everything. Ours: src/validation/script.lisp:573-650. Core at d3056bc: core_io.cpp:357-401; script/script.cpp:23-44.
fix_shape: Give DISASSEMBLE-SCRIPT Core's two rules and one flag. For a push of four bytes or fewer, render the CScriptNum value in decimal - the minimal-encoding sign convention is already implemented for script execution (%script-num), so the renderer should call it rather than grow a second one, and note Core passes fRequireMinimal=false here so a non-minimal push still renders. For opcodes, special-case OP_0, OP_1NEGATE and OP_1..OP_16 to '0', '-1' and '1'..'16' ahead of the *OPCODE-NAMES* lookup, leaving the table alone since other callers use it for real names. Then add the fAttemptSighashDecode parameter, default NIL: when true and the script is not unspendable, a push passing the existing CheckSignatureEncoding gets its last byte looked up in Core's mapSigHashTypes and replaced by '[ALL]'/'[NONE]'/'[SINGLE]' with the ANYONECANPAY variants. Pass it true from every scriptSig rendering site (tx-to-json's input-to-json, the PSBT decoders) and false from every scriptPubKey site, which is the split Core makes in TxToUniv.
